aisles.decision: Choose organic meat and eggs with pasture-raising certification, checking grass-fed wording on organ meats.
Choose wild seafood with a species label, live shellfish with closing shells, and dry scallops.
Choose plain whole cultured dairy with milk and cultures listed, and cream without additives.
Choose sealed organic foods with grain, nut, sweetener or oil named, and stated BPA-free can linings.
Choose organic sourdough or sprouted bread with whole grain named first, without enriched flour.
Read snack ingredients for named foods and oils, skipping natural flavors and added syrups.
Choose organic condiments listing vegetables, vinegar, salt, spices and any oil by name.
Choose plain water or organic kombucha in glass, checking for added sugar or natural flavors.

picks.decision: Grass-fed, grass-finished beef jerky with simple ingredients.
picks.avoid: Skip jerky listing liquid smoke or smoke flavoring.

picks.title: Venison
picks.decision: Venison in a tray naming deer.

picks.title: Flavored yogurt
picks.decision: Skip sweetened or flavored yogurt; choose plain whole yogurt.

picks.title: Dairy cream
picks.decision: Organic cream: certified organic feed and outdoor access; cream alone in ingredients.

picks.title: Non-dairy creamer
picks.decision: Skip non-dairy creamer; choose plain dairy cream.

picks.title: Cheese food slices
picks.decision: Skip cheese food slices; choose slices labeled cheese.
Look for butter listing cream and salt instead of margarine.

sources.name: Dr. Cate Shanahan: The Hateful Eight seed oils

picks.decision: Look for plain cream to whip instead of imitation whipped topping.

sources.name: Cornell LII: 7 CFR § 205.238 Organic livestock hormone rules
Cornucopia Institute: Carrageenan report and buyer’s guide
Weston A. Price Foundation: FAQ, dairy
CSPI Chemical Cuisine: food additive safety ratings

picks.title: Vegetable oil blend
picks.decision: Skip vegetable oil blends; choose a single named olive oil.

picks.title: Avocado oil
picks.decision: Organic virgin avocado oil with a harvest or production date.

picks.title: Whole grains
picks.decision: Organic whole grains with one grain named in the ingredients.

picks.title: Dried pulses
picks.decision: Organic dried lentils or split peas with one legume listed.

picks.title: Dry pasta
picks.decision: Organic whole-wheat pasta with semolina named and no enriched flour.

picks.title: Molasses
picks.decision: Organic molasses with molasses listed before other sweeteners.

picks.title: Date and coconut sugar
picks.decision: Organic date or coconut sweeteners named by their plant.

picks.title: Refined syrups
picks.decision: Skip corn, agave and brown rice syrups; choose pure maple syrup.

picks.title: Nuts and seeds
picks.decision: Organic raw nuts and seeds in sealed packages.

picks.title: Canned vegetables and fish
picks.decision: Organic canned foods with stated BPA-free lining and simple ingredients.

picks.title: Jarred vegetable sauces
picks.decision: Organic jarred vegetable sauces with named oil, salt and spices.

picks.title: Soy sauce
picks.decision: Organic naturally fermented or brewed soy sauce.
Water over juice; otherwise pasteurized, no warning label, no dyes, no added color.
picks.avoid: Skip juice drinks listing benzoates, benzoic acid, BVO or artificial color.

picks.decision: Look for plain water without flavors or sweeteners instead of soda.
sources: ANSES “The caps of glass bottles contaminate beverages with microplastics” https://www.anses.fr/en/content/caps-glass-bottles-contaminate-beverages-microplastics (water averaged 4.5 particles per liter in glass bottles and 1.6 in plastic bottles and cartons; particles matched the paint on the caps; 287 particles per liter with uncleaned caps fell to 106 when caps were blown clean and 87 when blowing was followed by rinsing)

picks.title: Breakfast cereal
picks.decision: Skip extruded breakfast cereal; choose organic whole-grain hot cereal.
Ask your meat counter for grass-fed, grass-finished marrow or knuckle soup bones.

sources.name: MSU Extension: Are you throwing away valuable food? Part three: Meat

picks.decision: Organic sausage: certified organic feed and outdoor access, with a third-party welfare seal.
picks.avoid: Skip sausage listing mechanically separated chicken, turkey or pork.

picks.decision: Wild pollock fish sticks made from fillet, not minced pieces.
picks.avoid: Skip Vietnam swai or basa; critics call ‘MSC certified’ a low bar.
Pass on cucumbers coated with wax, shellac or carnauba.
Skip cans without a BPA-free lining stated on the label.

organ_meats.decision: Organic organ meats from pasture-raised animals.
organ_meats.why: Organ meats and grass-fed sourcing: see Beef.
organ_meats.tier_note: The use-by date is a storage fact: organ meats keep only 1 to 2 days chilled; time outdoors on pasture, audited only with a certifier’s seal.

beef_veal.decision: Pasture-raised veal with a humane seal.
beef_veal.why: Pasture-raised veal means calves raised on open pasture beside the mother, never in feedlots.
beef_veal.instead: Pasture-raised veal with a humane seal.
beef_veal.tier_note: The veal systems are documented welfare categories; pasture with the mother is the whole-food standard; time outdoors on pasture, audited only with a certifier’s seal.

chicken_breast.decision: Organic, pasture-raised chicken breast, bone-in and skin-on.
chicken_breast.why: Certified Humane pasture raised requires 108 square feet per bird outdoors, matching AWA.

bacon.decision: Pasture-raised bacon with pork, salt and celery powder.
bacon.why: The USDA rule lets “Uncured” appear in the name only for products cured without synthetic nitrite.

ham.decision: Uncured whole-muscle ham with pork and salt.
ham.why: “Uncured” must lead the product name under federal curing rules.
ham.tier_note: Uncured is regulated wording at the start of the product name, not a pasture certification.
ham.cart_pick: Ham with a short curing list

turkey_bacon.decision: Uncured turkey bacon with turkey listed first.
turkey_bacon.why: 9 CFR 317.17 requires the term Uncured before the product name on products cured without nitrite.
turkey_bacon.cart_pick: Turkey bacon with named curing ingredients

cured_pork.decision: Dry-cured pork with pork and salt only.
cured_pork.why: “Uncured” wording is regulated product-name text for cured meats.
cured_pork.cart_pick: Sliced prosciutto with pork and salt

deli_meat_uncured.decision: Uncured deli meat sliced from a whole piece.
deli_meat_uncured.why: The word “Uncured” must precede the product name on cured-style meats.

egg_labels.decision: Organic eggs with a Certified Humane Pasture Raised seal.
egg_labels.why: Pasture raised under Certified Humane means 108 square feet per hen versus 2 for free range.

label_cage_free.decision: Pasture-raised eggs with an outdoor-access certification.
label_cage_free.why: Certified Humane free range needs 2 square feet outdoors; cage-free carries no outdoor figure.
label_cage_free.instead: Pasture-raised eggs with an outdoor-access certification.

label_pasture_raised_feed.decision: Organic pasture-raised eggs with Certified Humane or AWA certification.
label_pasture_raised_feed.why: Certified Humane and AWA pasture-raised standards both specify 108 square feet per bird.

sources.name: Cornucopia Institute: Organic Egg Scorecard Criteria

egg_duck_quail.decision: Pastured duck eggs in a carton naming duck.
egg_duck_quail.why: The Weston A. Price shopping guide lists pastured duck eggs among its best eggs.
egg_duck_quail.tier_note: Pastured is carton wording about outdoor access; organic adds certified feed.

seafood_certifications.decision: Wild seafood with the MSC fish checkmark and chain-of-custody code.
seafood_certifications.why: The MSC mark is only for wild fish from certified fisheries.
seafood_certifications.tier_note: The blue MSC symbol and tracking code identify a certified fishery, not freshness.

canned_tuna.decision: Pole-caught, troll-caught, FAD-free or school-caught canned tuna.
canned_tuna.why: Seafood Watch points to canned tuna with pole-caught, troll-caught, FAD-free, free school or school-caught on the label.

canned_fish_choosing.decision: Wild canned sardines with skin and bones in olive oil.
canned_fish_choosing.why: Weston A. Price recommends sardines with skin and bones as high in vitamin D and a good source of calcium.

mercury_by_fish.decision: Choose sardines with the fish named on the can.
mercury_by_fish.why: A Weston A. Price article lists sardines among a short list of recommended fish for low mercury.

seafood_fish_roe.decision: Salmon roe with only roe and salt.
seafood_fish_roe.why: Weston A. Price calls roe a rich source of vitamins A and D, very long-chain fatty acids, and zinc.

scallops.decision: Dry or dry-packed scallops, with no phosphate or water listed.
scallops.why: Dry scallops have not been soaked in sodium tripolyphosphate; skip milky liquid pooling in the tray.

crab.why: Foodal advises choosing live crabs that are active and moving, and heavy in the hand.

clams_mussels_oysters.decision: Live shellfish with a tag, closed shells and none cracked.
clams_mussels_oysters.why: Pacific Coast Shellfish Growers say oysters should always be tightly closed and mussels should close when tapped.

yogurt_plain_vs_flavored.decision: Organic plain whole yogurt with milk and named cultures.
yogurt_plain_vs_flavored.why: Organic yogurt can still contain added sugar; plain whole tubs are the pick, with grass-fed naming the milk source.
yogurt_plain_vs_flavored.tier_note: Plain means no added sugar, so sweeten it at home with fruit or honey; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

plain_kefir.decision: Organic whole-milk kefir with milk and cultures only.
plain_kefir.why: WAPF rates plain, whole yogurt and kefir without added vitamins, preferably grass-fed, as good.
plain_kefir.tier_note: Milk and cultures alone is the whole-food reading of a kefir bottle; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

sour_cream.decision: Organic sour cream with cream and cultures only.
sour_cream.why: Grass-fed names the feeding standard; wAPF lists sour cream with additives, and homogenized cream, under avoid.
sour_cream.tier_note: Live cultures do the souring here; acidified tubs are soured with added acids, and 100% grass-fed means the cows ate grass and hay, never grain; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

grassfed_butter.decision: Organic butter with cream and salt, without natural flavors.
grassfed_butter.why: WAPF rates pasteurized butter without natural flavors, preferably grass-fed, as good.
grassfed_butter.tier_note: Butter’s ingredient list shows whether the cream and salt have added natural flavors.
grassfed_butter.cart_pick: Organic butter with cream and salt

ghee.decision: Organic ghee with butterfat or clarified butter alone.
ghee.why: WAPF rates pasteurized ghee without natural flavors, preferably grass-fed, as good.
ghee.tier_note: Butter as the one ingredient is the whole-food reading of a ghee jar; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

cheese_real_vs_processed.decision: Organic cheese labeled cheese, without cheese-food or cheese-product wording.
cheese_real_vs_processed.why: Process cheese is ground and heated with other ingredients; grass-fed describes the milk source, not the cheese type.

cream_cheese.decision: Organic cream cheese without gums or added thickeners.
cream_cheese.why: Grass-fed names the milk source; WAPF favors whole cream cheese without additives.
cream_cheese.tier_note: A live culture on the list marks cream cheese made the traditional way; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

cottage_cheese.decision: Organic cottage cheese with named cultures and no gums.
cottage_cheese.why: Grass-fed names the milk source; WAPF favors whole cottage cheese without additives.
cottage_cheese.tier_note: A culture sets the best curd; a tub marked directly set was curdled with acid, and 100% grass-fed means the cows ate grass and hay, never grain; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

ice_cream.decision: Organic vanilla ice cream with cream, milk and egg yolks.
ice_cream.why: WAPF favors milk, cream, yolks and real vanilla; grass-fed names the dairy source, not the additives.
ice_cream.tier_note: The recipe reads off the list: cream, milk, sugar and yolks, no gums or oils, and 100% grass-fed means the cows ate grass and hay, never grain; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

canned_coconut_milk.decision: Organic canned coconut milk with coconut and water only.
canned_coconut_milk.why: WAPF recommends canned whole coconut milk without additives, preferably in BPA-free containers.

plant_butter.decision: Butter with cream and salt instead of vegetable-oil spreads.
plant_butter.why: WAPF avoid list covers spreads combining butter with vegetable oils and most commercial vegetable and seed oils.
plant_butter.instead: Butter with cream and salt instead of vegetable-oil spreads.

cooking_oils.decision: Organic cooking oil naming olive or coconut alone.
cooking_oils.why: The list names the fat. Avocado oil fits only when the maker states it is pure and pressed without heat.

olive_oil_grades.decision: Organic extra-virgin olive oil with a harvest date.
olive_oil_grades.why: Dark glass or tins protect oil from light; UC Davis names harvest dates as a freshness cue.

label_cold_pressed_expeller.decision: Organic olive or coconut oil, cold pressed or expeller pressed.
label_cold_pressed_expeller.why: Organic handling rules bar volatile synthetic solvents as processing aids.

sources.name: Dr. Cate Shanahan: The Hateful Eight seed oils

lard_tallow.decision: Organic lard or tallow with pasture or grass-fed wording.
lard_tallow.why: WAPF rates lard from pigs raised outdoors and tallow from grass-fed cows and sheep as best fats.

rancidity_check.decision: Organic oil in dark glass, without a stale-nut smell.
rancidity_check.why: UC Davis names stale nuts as a smell of rancid oil and clear plastic as least protective.
rancidity_check.tier_note: Clear bottles expose oil to light; stale-nut smells signal oxidation.

rice_arsenic.decision: Organic whole-grain rice with rice as the only ingredient.
rice_arsenic.why: WAPF rates organic whole grain rice among the best grains and lists white rice under avoid.
rice_arsenic.tier_note: Rice type and origin affect arsenic levels; skipping rice syrup is the buying standard.

grains_beyond_rice.decision: Organic quinoa, millet or buckwheat with one grain listed.
grains_beyond_rice.why: WAPF lists all non-organic grains and legumes under avoid; MSU Extension lists millet as a whole grain.
grains_beyond_rice.tier_note: An organic seal covers how the grain was grown, not how it was milled.

wild_rice.decision: Organic wild rice with no white-rice blend.
wild_rice.why: WAPF favors wildcrafted wild rice; MSU Extension classifies wild rice as a whole grain.

beans_dried_vs_canned.decision: Organic dried beans first, then cans with stated BPA-free lining.
beans_dried_vs_canned.why: WAPF rates organic dried beans as best and organic canned legumes as good, eaten only once or twice a month.

specialty_flours.decision: Organic alternative flours with one flour named.
specialty_flours.why: WAPF rates freshly ground, soaked organic whole grain flours as best and organic sprouted flours as good.

label_multigrain_vs_whole_grain.decision: Organic grains labeled whole grain, beyond multigrain wording.
label_multigrain_vs_whole_grain.why: Multigrain names a mix of grains; both MSU Extension and the Whole Grains Council say the mix may be refined.

sprouted_grain_bread.decision: Organic sprouted-grain bread with sprouted grains named first.
sprouted_grain_bread.why: Sprouted grains have begun to germinate; the first ingredient shows which grain leads the loaf.

sandwich_bread.decision: Organic sourdough or sprouted whole-grain sandwich bread.
sandwich_bread.why: WAPF lists white-flour breads with hydrogenated oils, added gluten, soy or additives under avoid.
sandwich_bread.instead: Organic sourdough or sprouted whole-grain sandwich bread.

gluten_free_bread.decision: Gluten-free bread with a named whole-grain flour first.
gluten_free_bread.why: “Whole” in the first ingredient suggests a mostly whole-grain product; the wording is not a guarantee.

sources.name: Whole Grains Council: Identifying whole grain products

gluten_free_bread.instead: Gluten-free bread with a named whole-grain flour first.

bagels.decision: Organic sourdough or sprouted bagels without ascorbic acid.
bagels.why: WAPF favors organic sourdough or sprouted breads and lists ascorbic acid under avoid.
bagels.instead: Organic sourdough or sprouted bagels without ascorbic acid.
bagels.tier_note: Skipping ascorbic acid in the ingredients is the bread standard here.

sugars.decision: Organic cane sugar named as dehydrated cane juice.
sugars.why: WAPF lists dehydrated sugar cane juice among best sweeteners and white sugar under avoid.

maple_syrup.decision: Organic pure maple syrup with no corn syrup.
maple_syrup.why: WAPF lists maple syrup as a best sweetener and imitation syrups under avoid.

nuts_raw_vs_roasted.decision: Organic raw nuts in sealed packs without sugar or coatings.
nuts_raw_vs_roasted.why: WAPF favors organic raw nuts in sealed packs and lists sugar, agave and added flavorings under avoid.

nut_butter_ingredients.decision: Organic nut butter with nuts and optional salt only.
nut_butter_ingredients.why: WAPF avoid list covers nut butters with hydrogenated oils, sugar, agave or flavorings.

seeds.decision: Organic raw seeds, one seed named in a sealed pack.
seeds.why: WAPF rates fresh organic raw seeds in sealed packages as best.
seeds.tier_note: The pack date is a freshness cue, never a safety rule.

trail_mix.decision: Organic plain nuts instead of sweetened or oil-coated trail mix.
trail_mix.why: WAPF avoid list names nut mixtures with partially hydrogenated oils, sugar, chocolate or flavorings.
trail_mix.instead: Organic plain nuts instead of sweetened or oil-coated trail mix.

pasta_sauce.decision: Organic pasta sauce with tomatoes first and no added sugar.
pasta_sauce.why: WAPF lists most commercial sauces, ketchup and other condiments under avoid.

seaweed.decision: Organic sea vegetables, named species and origin outside China.
seaweed.why: WAPF favors whole or powdered sea vegetables from outside China, including when certified organic.

hummus.decision: Organic hummus with chickpeas, tahini and olive oil.
hummus.why: The ingredient list identifies chickpeas, tahini and the named olive oil.

dried_herbs.decision: Organic single-herb jars without citric acid or MSG.
dried_herbs.why: WAPF avoid list covers spices and blends containing MSG, citric acid or hydrolyzed protein.

whole_spices.decision: Organic whole spices with one seed or stick named.
whole_spices.why: WAPF lists spices and blends containing MSG, citric acid, hydrolyzed protein or other additives under avoid.

salt.decision: Unrefined gray, pink, red or beige salt without iodized wording.
salt.why: WAPF lists unrefined salt in light gray, pink, red or beige as best and iodized salt as avoid.

baking_powder.decision: Aluminum-free baking powder in a labeled tin.
baking_powder.why: WAPF lists aluminum-free baking powder as best and baking powder containing aluminum under avoid.

raw_cider_vinegar.decision: Organic raw, unfiltered apple cider vinegar with visible mother.
raw_cider_vinegar.why: WAPF lists organic raw vinegars as best.

vinegar.decision: Apple cider, wine or balsamic vinegar, not distilled white.
vinegar.why: WAPF avoid list names distilled vinegar.
vinegar.instead: Apple cider, wine or balsamic vinegar instead of distilled white vinegar.

ketchup_mustard.decision: Organic mustard or fermented ketchup without natural flavors.
ketchup_mustard.why: WAPF lists organic mustard and organic fermented ketchup among best condiments.

condiments.decision: Mayonnaise or dressings with olive oil, not soy or canola.
condiments.why: WAPF avoid list names soy and canola oils.
condiments.instead: Mayonnaise or dressings with olive oil instead of soy or canola.
condiments.tier_note: The first oil listed is the one the jar mostly holds.

crackers.decision: Organic whole-grain crackers without hydrogenated oil or soy flour.
crackers.why: WAPF lists white-flour crackers with partially hydrogenated oils, soy flour or additives under avoid.
crackers.instead: Organic whole-grain crackers without hydrogenated oil or soy flour.

pretzels.decision: Whole-grain pretzels with whole flour listed first.
pretzels.why: WAPF lists white flour products under avoid.
pretzels.instead: Whole-grain pretzels with whole flour listed first.

rice_cakes_puffed_grains.decision: Organic whole-grain crackers instead of puffed rice cakes.
rice_cakes_puffed_grains.why: WAPF lists puffed grain products such as rice cakes under avoid.
rice_cakes_puffed_grains.instead: Organic whole-grain crackers instead of puffed rice cakes.

bottled_water_buying.decision: Bottled spring water with spring water printed on the label.
bottled_water_buying.why: Spring water must come from the spring or a bore hole tapping the underground formation feeding it.

kombucha.decision: Organic kombucha with black tea in a glass bottle.
kombucha.why: WAPF recommends organic lacto-fermented beverages in glass jars, such as kombucha made with organic black tea.

coconut_water.decision: Organic coconut water with coconut water alone, outside aseptic boxes.
coconut_water.why: WAPF lists coconut products in aseptic boxes under avoid.
coconut_water.tier_note: A single ingredient and the absence of aseptic boxes are visible package checks.

beef_grassfed_vs_grainfed.decision: Organic grass-finished beef with the AGA Grassfed seal.
beef_grassfed_vs_grainfed.why: Grass after weaning, no grain and no feedlot. A grass finish gives you leaner beef with a different fat balance.

beef_cuts_basics.decision: Grass-fed organic whole beef cuts with AGA certification.
beef_cuts_basics.tier_note: The ‘mechanically tenderized’ name is federal label text; an untouched whole cut is held as a standard; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

ground_beef_lean_ratio.decision: Organic grass-finished ground beef with its lean ratio printed.
ground_beef_lean_ratio.why: Ground beef and grass-fed sourcing: see Beef.

hot_dogs.decision: Grass-fed beef hot dogs, AGA seal and short ingredient list.
hot_dogs.why: AGA animals are fed only grass and forage and never given added growth hormones.

lamb_goat.decision: Organic lamb or goat with an AWA pasture seal.
lamb_goat.cart_pick: Organic lamb or goat with an AWA seal

bison.decision: Organic AGA-certified bison with bison alone listed.
bison.why: AGA requires a 100% grass diet from weaning until harvest.
bison.tier_note: Many bison finish on grain; “grass-fed” is the producer’s own word unless a certifier’s seal audits it; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

chicken_cuts_basics.decision: Organic whole chicken, AWA certified, without basting solution.
chicken_cuts_basics.why: AWA guarantees outdoor pasture life for the whole animal.

poultry_chicken_wings.decision: Organic pasture-raised chicken wings with intact skin and no coating.
poultry_chicken_wings.why: Plain skin-on wings keep the cut intact; organic livestock rules require certified organic feed.

rotisserie_chicken.decision: Rotisserie chicken listing only chicken and salt.

sources.name: Dr. Cate Shanahan: The Hateful Eight seed oils

rotisserie_chicken.why: Chicken and salt keep the recipe simple; the organic seal identifies certified organic livestock feed.
rotisserie_chicken.tier_note: The sticker lists added starches and sweeteners; organic means certified organic feed and outdoor access.

turkey_whole.decision: Organic whole turkey with pasture-raising certification.
turkey_whole.why: An unbasted whole bird avoids added basting solution; organic rules require certified organic feed.
turkey_whole.tier_note: Pasture-raised turkey: time outdoors on pasture, audited only with a certifier’s seal; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

ground_turkey.decision: Organic ground turkey listing breast and thigh meat only.
ground_turkey.why: Breast and thigh alone identify the meat in the pack; antibiotic-treated birds cannot be sold as organic.

poultry_duck.decision: Organic whole duck with skin on and an AWA seal.
poultry_duck.why: AWA covers duck standards and requires pasture or range living.
poultry_duck.tier_note: Pasture-raised duck: time outdoors on pasture, audited only with a certifier’s seal; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

pork_cuts_and_enhanced.decision: Organic pasture-raised pork chops without added solution.
pork_cuts_and_enhanced.why: AWA guarantees pigs live outdoors on pasture or range.

salmon_wild_vs_farmed.decision: Wild salmon, frozen wild Alaskan before fresh farmed.
salmon_wild_vs_farmed.why: Wild is a whole-food preference; read the species name, with deep-red flesh identifying sockeye.

label_wild_vs_farm_raised.decision: Wild fish with country and catch method on the tag.
label_wild_vs_farm_raised.why: Wild is the seafood premise; the production-method label distinguishes wild from farm-raised fish.

farmed_fish_by_species.decision: Farmed fish carrying the ASC logo on the pack.
farmed_fish_by_species.why: ASC says seafood carrying its label on pack was farmed with care.

shrimp_imported_vs_domestic.decision: Wild Gulf or US shrimp, shell on, without additives.
shrimp_imported_vs_domestic.why: Shell-on shrimp without additives keep the product close to the catch; the origin label names the country.

white_fish.decision: Wild-caught white fish by its named species, firm, mild-smelling.
white_fish.why: Wild Pacific cod is the pick; its gray or brown skin and paler belly provide a visible species check.

seafood_fresh_sardines_mackerel.decision: Wild sardines with shiny skin or mackerel with vivid stripes.
seafood_fresh_sardines_mackerel.why: Mackerel color fades quickly after death, so dull stripes signal age.
seafood_fresh_sardines_mackerel.science: Sardines and mackerel are high in the fats EPA and DHA. Small fish are less likely to carry mercury or PCBs. Most ocean fish have more selenium than mercury; king mackerel and swordfish are exceptions. Small fish eaten whole with their bones supply calcium and vitamin D.
seafood_fresh_sardines_mackerel.detail: Sardines and mackerel rank high in the omega-3 fats EPA and DHA. Small fish low on the food chain are less likely to carry mercury or PCBs, and sardines are eaten whole with their tiny bones, which adds calcium and vitamin D. Most ocean fish carry more selenium than mercury; king mackerel and swordfish are the exceptions. Cooked fresh mackerel bones are too sharp to eat, unlike the softened bones in canned mackerel. Fresh sardines can be hard to find, so ask the counter.

lobster.decision: A live lobster that moves, or hard-frozen tails.
lobster.why: Moving claws identify a live lobster; frozen tails should feel hard without ice glaze.
lobster.tier_note: Active claws show a live lobster; hard tails and ice glaze are frozen-product checks.

smoked_salmon.decision: Wild-caught smoked salmon, nova or lox, kept cold.
smoked_salmon.why: Read origin and wild or farm-raised wording on chilled salmon; these name production, not the smoking process.

seafood_counter.decision: Whole fish on ice, clear eyes and a species sign.
seafood_counter.why: Whole fish on ice should look bright-eyed with shiny skin, as the sardine guidance describes.
seafood_counter.tier_note: Clear eyes, ice and a species sign are visible counter checks.

whole_vs_reduced_fat_milk.decision: Organic whole milk without ultra-pasteurized wording near the date.
sources: University of Minnesota Extension “A2 milk and A2 genetics” https://extension.umn.edu/agriculture/animals-and-livestock/dairy/a2-milk-and-a2-genetics

Michigan State University Extension, dairy processing article https://www.canr.msu.edu/news/they_did_what_to_your_milk (homogenization forces milk at high pressure through small holes so fat does not rise; no health benefits or risks associated with it; non-homogenized milk available from some bottlers)
whole_vs_reduced_fat_milk.why: Whole milk keeps its milkfat; WAPF favors grass-fed dairy and lists ultra-pasteurized milk under avoid.
whole_vs_reduced_fat_milk.tier_note: Vat, or low-temp, pasteurizing holds milk at 145°F for 30 minutes; regular gets 161°F for 15 seconds; certified organic feed and outdoor access.

oats_steelcut_rolled_instant.decision: Organic whole-grain oats without flavorings or added sugar.

sources.name: Cornucopia Institute: Glyphosate Used to Kill and Prepare Crops for Harvest

oats_steelcut_rolled_instant.why: Whole oats keep the grain intact; organic farming bars glyphosate, and soaking is a traditional preparation.

cornmeal_polenta_grits.decision: Organic whole-grain cornmeal or grits without degerminated wording.
cornmeal_polenta_grits.why: Corn is on the Non-GMO Project High-Risk List; degerminated cornmeal is not a whole grain.

flour_basics.decision: Organic whole-wheat flour without bleached or enriched wording.
flour_basics.why: WAPF says avoid white flour and white flour products, and lists bleached white flour under avoid.

sourdough.why: WAPF favors sourdough from organic whole grain flour; fermentation changes the grain.

honey_adulteration.decision: Organic raw, unfiltered honey with pollen left in the jar.
honey_adulteration.why: WAPF lists raw honey, preferably unfiltered, among its best sweeteners; ultra-filtration removes pollen.

snack_bars.decision: Whole nuts or fruit instead of syrup-bound or soy-isolate bars.

sources.name: Weston A. Price Foundation: Snack Attack

snack_bars.why: WAPF lists brown rice syrup and agave under avoid; whole nuts or fruit keep the snack ingredients recognizable.
snack_bars.instead: Whole nuts or fruit instead of syrup-bound or soy-isolate bars.
snack_bars.tier_note: Skipping brown rice syrup and agave is the snack standard, read directly from ingredients.

snacks.decision: Organic potato or corn chips, olive or coconut oil, salt.
snacks.why: WAPF lists most commercial vegetable and seed oils under avoid and olive and organic virgin coconut oil among best.
snacks.tier_note: Potato flour and vegetable powder are visible ingredient checks for veggie chips.

do_lines.organ_meats: Check liver or heart packs for an AGA or organic seal.
do_lines.beef_veal: Read the label for pasture rearing and a humane seal.
do_lines.chicken_breast: Find the Certified Humane Pasture Raised seal alongside USDA certification.
do_lines.bacon: Find the pasture seal on the bacon pack.
do_lines.ham: Read the product name’s opening word for Uncured, then check for pork and salt.
do_lines.turkey_bacon: Read the name for Uncured, then check which meat leads the ingredient list.
do_lines.cured_pork: Read the ingredients for pork and salt alone.
do_lines.deli_meat_uncured: Ask for fresh slices from a whole roast bearing an Uncured label.
do_lines.egg_labels: Find USDA Organic on the carton beside the other seal.
do_lines.label_cage_free: Skip cartons claiming cage-free without a seal for outdoor access.
do_lines.label_pasture_raised_feed: Check both claims for seals: AWA Pasture Raised plus USDA Organic.
do_lines.egg_duck_quail: Read the carton for duck and pastured wording.
do_lines.seafood_certifications: Check the MSC program name, blue fish symbol and tracking code.
do_lines.canned_tuna: Read the catch wording for pole, troll, FAD-free or school methods.
do_lines.canned_fish_choosing: Read the species name and check for fish, water or olive oil.
do_lines.mercury_by_fish: Check the species name on the can for sardines.
do_lines.seafood_fish_roe: Read the jar for salmon roe and salt alone.
do_lines.scallops: Check the tray for milky pooling; look for dry-packed on the label.
do_lines.crab: Watch for leg movement before picking a live crab.
do_lines.clams_mussels_oysters: Tap to check that each shell shuts, then find the bag’s harvest tag.
do_lines.yogurt_plain_vs_flavored: Read for milk and culture names; skip sugar, pectin or flavors.
do_lines.plain_kefir: Read the kefir ingredients for milk and cultures alone.
do_lines.sour_cream: Skip tubs listing starch, gums or flavor words beside cream and cultures.
do_lines.grassfed_butter: Read for cream and salt; skip any natural flavor entry.
do_lines.ghee: Check the jar lists one dairy fat, without oil blended in.
do_lines.cheese_real_vs_processed: Read the printed name; skip cheese followed by food or product.
do_lines.cream_cheese: Read the list for cream, milk, salt and cultures.
do_lines.cottage_cheese: Read for milk and cream first; skip thickening gums.
do_lines.ice_cream: Read for cream, milk, yolks and real vanilla; skip flavor words or extenders.
do_lines.canned_coconut_milk: Check the can’s lining claim for BPA-free alongside a two-ingredient list.
do_lines.plant_butter: Skip spreads listing palm, canola or a vegetable oil blend.
do_lines.cooking_oils: Check the bottle names one oil, without a blend.
do_lines.olive_oil_grades: Choose a dark bottle or metal tin; skip clear plastic.
do_lines.label_cold_pressed_expeller: Read the bottle’s pressing method: cold or expeller.
do_lines.lard_tallow: Read for a single fat and pastured wording on the label.
do_lines.rancidity_check: Skip clear bottles; check for a paint-and-crayon smell when opening oil.
do_lines.rice_arsenic: Check the origin on the bag; skip brown rice syrup.
do_lines.grains_beyond_rice: Check the grain bag for a single ingredient and an organic seal.
do_lines.wild_rice: Read for wild rice alone, without white rice blended in.
do_lines.beans_dried_vs_canned: Read dry bags for beans alone; check tins for a BPA-free claim.
do_lines.specialty_flours: Count the types of flour listed; choose one with organic on the bag.
do_lines.label_multigrain_vs_whole_grain: Read for 100% whole grain, or whole before the grain name.
do_lines.sprouted_grain_bread: Read for sprouted before each grain; skip loaves listing flour first.
do_lines.sandwich_bread: Read the list’s top; skip enriched wheat flour, sugar or soybean oil.
do_lines.gluten_free_bread: Read the flours in ingredient order; skip unless the first is marked whole.
do_lines.bagels: Check the ingredients for ascorbic acid; ask about the water bath.
do_lines.sugars: Read for dehydrated cane juice, beyond sugar alone.
do_lines.maple_syrup: Read for pure maple syrup alone; skip corn syrup in the ingredients.
do_lines.nuts_raw_vs_roasted: Find raw on the sealed pack; skip sugared or coated nuts.
do_lines.nut_butter_ingredients: Read the list for nuts and salt; skip sugar, palm or hydrogenated oils.
do_lines.seeds: Check the raw seed pack’s date and single-ingredient list.
do_lines.trail_mix: Skip mixes listing sugar, chocolate or vegetable oil beside the nuts.
do_lines.pasta_sauce: Check that tomatoes lead, with oil named and no sugar or natural flavors.
do_lines.seaweed: Read the sea vegetable’s name and country; skip packs from China.
do_lines.hummus: Read the ingredients for canola or soybean oil; skip either.
do_lines.dried_herbs: Read for one herb; skip blends listing citric acid or MSG.
do_lines.whole_spices: Pick intact seeds or sticks, rather than a ground blend.
do_lines.salt: Look for gray, pink, red or beige crystals; skip iodized on the label.
do_lines.baking_powder: Read the tin for an explicit no-aluminum claim.
do_lines.raw_cider_vinegar: Check the bottle’s bottom for cloudy strands of mother.
do_lines.vinegar: Read for apple cider, wine or balsamic on the label.
do_lines.ketchup_mustard: Read the list for tomatoes, vinegar and spices.
do_lines.condiments: Skip jars naming soybean or canola as the first oil.
do_lines.crackers: Read for white flour, hydrogenated oil or soy flour; skip any listed.
do_lines.pretzels: Read the first ingredient; skip refined white flour.
do_lines.rice_cakes_puffed_grains: Skip flavor-coated grains or packs listing natural flavor or syrup.
do_lines.bottled_water_buying: Read the water source on the label; look for spring.
do_lines.kombucha: Check the glass bottle for organic wording and black tea in the ingredients.
do_lines.coconut_water: Read the ingredient line; skip aseptic boxes and added sugar.
do_lines.beef_grassfed_vs_grainfed: Find the AGA seal and 100% grass-fed wording.
do_lines.beef_cuts_basics: Check the tray’s seal and the AGA and USDA marks.
do_lines.ground_beef_lean_ratio: Find the lean ratio beside the AGA seal on the pack.
do_lines.hot_dogs: Find the AGA seal, then count the ingredients.
do_lines.lamb_goat: Look for pale pink fat on chops carrying the AWA pasture stamp.
do_lines.bison: Read the pack for bison alone and the AGA mark beside the cut.
do_lines.chicken_cuts_basics: Check for cream-yellow skin and an AWA seal on the bird.
do_lines.poultry_chicken_wings: Check that the skin has no tears, then read the raising claims.
do_lines.rotisserie_chicken: Read the ingredient list for added starches or sweeteners.
do_lines.turkey_whole: Read the tag for not basted and Certified Humane Pasture Raised.
do_lines.ground_turkey: Read for thigh and breast meat alone, then check the certification seal.
do_lines.poultry_duck: Pick a whole bird with skin on and an AWA seal.
do_lines.pork_cuts_and_enhanced: Find an AWA or Certified Humane pasture seal on the chop pack.
do_lines.salmon_wild_vs_farmed: Read for wild Alaskan, then check the flesh for a deep red color.
do_lines.label_wild_vs_farm_raised: Read the tag for wild or farm-raised, plus origin and catch details.
do_lines.farmed_fish_by_species: Find the ASC logo on the fish pack.
do_lines.shrimp_imported_vs_domestic: Read the bag for Gulf or US wild origin; check for shells.
do_lines.white_fish: Turn the fillet to check its gray-brown skin, then read the cod tag.
do_lines.seafood_fresh_sardines_mackerel: Check these fish for bright stripes or shiny skin.
do_lines.lobster: Check claw movement; choose frozen tails that feel hard without ice glaze.
do_lines.smoked_salmon: Check the cold case, then read the label for origin and wild wording.
do_lines.seafood_counter: Check the counter for clear eyes, ice and a species sign.
do_lines.whole_vs_reduced_fat_milk: Read beside the date; skip ultra-pasteurized and check the fat wording.
do_lines.oats_steelcut_rolled_instant: Skip instant packets listing flavor or sugar; read for whole grain oats.
do_lines.cornmeal_polenta_grits: Find the USDA seal; skip degerminated on the grain bag.
do_lines.flour_basics: Read the bag for whole wheat before choosing flour.
do_lines.sourdough: Find a starter or culture in the bread’s ingredient list.
do_lines.honey_adulteration: Look through the jar for cloudiness from pollen, rather than clear honey.
do_lines.snack_bars: Read ingredients for brown rice syrup or agave; skip bars listing either.
do_lines.snacks: Read for potatoes or corn, olive or coconut oil, and salt alone.
